accepted.s: Under Section 84(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Apex Council for the Krishna and Godavari rivers was constituted by the Centre from which date?
o: The date of constitution of the two River Management Boards
The date of publication of the tribunal awards
The date of enactment of the Act
accepted.x: Section 84(1) provides for constitution of the Apex Council by the Centre from the appointed day.
accepted.tq: Recall the statutory trigger date rather than the date of a later institutional action.
accepted.sec: Apex Council - composition, chairperson, functions (APRA Sec. 84)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Apex Council constituted under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. It consists of three members in all.
2. The Union Minister of Water Resources is its Chairperson.
3. The Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Apex Council has three members: the Union Minister of Water Resources as Chairperson and the Chief Ministers of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana as members.
accepted.tq: Use the composition count and identify the office-holders before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Apex Council - composition, chairperson, functions (APRA Sec. 84)

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Apex Council under Section 84(3) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Referring disputes not covered by KWDT to a tribunal under the ISRWD Act, 1956
Allocating or redetermining the shares of the States in river waters
Approving new projects on the Krishna and Godavari after appraisal by the Board and the CWC
Supervising the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards
accepted.x: The Apex Council can supervise the Boards, approve new projects after appraisal, settle disputes by negotiation and refer certain disputes to a tribunal. Allocation or redetermination of shares is not stated as its function here.
accepted.tq: Separate the power to approve projects and settle disputes from the power to allocate water shares.
accepted.sec: Apex Council - composition, chairperson, functions (APRA Sec. 84)

accepted.s: The power to approve a new project on the Krishna or Godavari, after appraisal by the concerned Board and the Central Water Commission, belongs to which body?
o: The Krishna River Management Board alone
The Godavari River Management Board alone
accepted.x: Under Section 84(3), approval of new Krishna or Godavari projects after the prescribed appraisal is a function of the Apex Council.
accepted.tq: Use the authority-based trap by distinguishing the Apex Council from the subordinate Boards.
accepted.sec: Apex Council - composition, chairperson, functions (APRA Sec. 84)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the role of the Apex Council in relation to disputes?
o: It settles disputes by negotiation and may refer disputes not covered by KWDT to a tribunal under the ISRWD Act, 1956.
It permanently reallocates all river-water shares without reference to any tribunal.
It refers every dispute directly to the Supreme Court without negotiation.
It deals only with disputes concerning the Tungabhadra River.
accepted.x: The Apex Council is empowered to settle disputes through negotiation and to refer disputes not covered by KWDT to a tribunal under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional power with the correct sequence of negotiation followed by possible tribunal reference.
accepted.sec: Apex Council - composition, chairperson, functions (APRA Sec. 84)

accepted.s: Under Section 85(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Krishna River Management Board and Godavari River Management Board were to be set up within how many days of the appointed day?
accepted.x: Section 85(1) required the two Boards to be set up within 60 days of the appointed day.
accepted.tq: Test the exact statutory time limit using close numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the headquarters arrangement under Section 85(2) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: KRMB in Telangana and GRMB in Andhra Pradesh
KRMB in Andhra Pradesh and GRMB in Telangana
Both KRMB and GRMB in Andhra Pradesh
Both KRMB and GRMB in Telangana
accepted.x: The Krishna River Management Board has its headquarters in Andhra Pradesh, while the Godavari River Management Board has its headquarters in Telangana.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two similarly structured Boards by pairing each Board with its headquarters.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Krishna River Management Board and the Godavari River Management Board:
1. They are autonomous bodies under the administrative control of the Centre.
2. Each Board includes a Chairperson from the Centre.
3. Each State provides two members, one technical and one administrative.
4. Each Board has one central expert and a full-time Member Secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Sections 85(3) and 85(4) provide for autonomous Boards under Central administrative control, with the stated Chairperson, State members, central expert and full-time Member Secretary.
accepted.tq: Build the answer by checking each component of the statutory composition and status.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s: Which provision requires CISF guards to protect the reservoirs connected with the Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards?
accepted.x: Section 85(7) provides for CISF guards for the reservoirs under the Board arrangement.
accepted.tq: Test exact section-number recall from a cluster of closely related Section 85 provisions.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the administration and jurisdiction of the KRMB and GRMB:
1. Staff are to be taken on deputation from both States equally.
2. The States are responsible for funding the Boards.
3. The Boards have jurisdiction over projects notified by the Centre.
4. The Boards may make regulations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Section 86 deals with equal deputation and State funding, Section 87 with jurisdiction over projects notified by the Centre, and Section 88 with the power to make regulations.
accepted.tq: Group provisions by subject—staff and finance, jurisdiction, and regulation—before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s: Which Ministry notified the jurisdiction of both the Krishna River Management Board and the Godavari River Management Board in July 2021?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: The Ministry of Jal Shakti notified the jurisdiction of both Boards in July 2021.
accepted.tq: Apply the department-swapping trap by identifying the ministry directly associated with water resources.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes a function of the KRMB and GRMB under Schedule XI?
o: Abolishing the awards of the water-dispute tribunals
Approving all new river projects without appraisal by any other body
Redetermining the shares of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in every water year
Regulating supply from notified headworks according to tribunal awards
accepted.x: The Boards regulate supply from notified headworks in accordance with tribunal awards, release water according to State shares and advise on floods and droughts. Allocating or redetermining shares is not their function.
accepted.tq: Distinguish operational regulation from the separate power of allocating or redetermining shares.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s: A State fails to comply with the directions applicable to a River Management Board. Under Section 92 read with Schedule XI, which consequence may follow?
o: Financial and other penalties imposed by the Centre
Automatic dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly
Cancellation of the relevant tribunal award by the Board
Transfer of all State water projects to the Supreme Court
accepted.x: A defaulting State may face financial and other penalties from the Centre under Section 92 and Schedule XI.
accepted.tq: Identify the consequence linked to non-compliance without confusing it with judicial or constitutional sanctions.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s: In August 2026, the three-member committee of the KRMB permitted which use of water from Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar in view of El Niño and poor inflows?
accepted.x: The KRMB’s three-member committee allowed only drinking-water use from Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar because of El Niño and poor inflows.
accepted.tq: Use the current-affairs application by linking the water restriction to the stated hydrological conditions.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s: The KRMB advised Telangana in September 2026 after the storage in which reservoir fell because of power generation?
accepted.x: The KRMB advised Telangana after storage in the Srisailam reservoir fell due to its power generation.
accepted.tq: Use location-specific recall for a current water-management development.
accepted.sec: KRMB and GRMB - headquarters, sections, jurisdiction, status, functions

accepted.s: The 2014 ad hoc division of the undivided Andhra Pradesh share of 811 TMC of Krishna water between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana was in which ratio?
accepted.x: The ad hoc division was 66:34 in the ratio of Andhra Pradesh to Telangana, corresponding approximately to 512 TMC and 299 TMC respectively.
accepted.tq: Test the exact ratio and avoid replacing the ad hoc division with the later demand for equal sharing.
accepted.sec: Krishna water ad hoc sharing ratio between AP and Telangana

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the approximate TMC allocation under the 2014 ad hoc division of 811 TMC between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
o: Andhra Pradesh 560 TMC and Telangana 251 TMC
Andhra Pradesh 299 TMC and Telangana 512 TMC
Andhra Pradesh 512 TMC and Telangana 299 TMC
Andhra Pradesh 405 TMC and Telangana 406 TMC
accepted.x: The 66:34 ad hoc division of 811 TMC gave approximately 512 TMC to Andhra Pradesh and 299 TMC to Telangana.
accepted.tq: Convert the stated ratio into the corresponding quantities and watch for reversal of State names.
accepted.sec: Krishna water ad hoc sharing ratio between AP and Telangana

accepted.s: Telangana’s demand for a 50:50 division of Krishna waters was principally based on which claim?
o: Its exclusive control over the Krishna River’s headwaters
The 1980 Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal award
Its greater number of coastal districts
accepted.x: Telangana demanded equal sharing while citing its larger basin area as the basis for the claim.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated basis of a policy demand rather than the legal response to it.
accepted.sec: Krishna water ad hoc sharing ratio between AP and Telangana

accepted.s: Why did Andhra Pradesh reject Telangana’s demand for a 50:50 division of Krishna waters at the CWC-chaired committee?
o: It accepted the demand but deferred implementation until 2030.
It considered the demand contrary to KWDT awards and Apex Council decisions.
It argued that the Krishna River had ceased to be an inter-State river.
It considered the demand contrary only to the Godavari Tribunal award.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh rejected the demand on the ground that it was contrary to the KWDT awards and decisions of the Apex Council.
accepted.tq: Link the policy position to the legal and institutional grounds stated for rejecting it.
accepted.sec: Krishna water ad hoc sharing ratio between AP and Telangana

accepted.s: Justice R.S. Bachawat was the Chairperson of which pair of tribunals?
accepted.x: Justice R.S. Bachawat chaired KWDT-I and the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal, whereas KWDT-II was chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between tribunal chairpersons by matching the repeated name with the correct two tribunals.
accepted.sec: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

accepted.s: The final award of the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal-I was given in which year?
accepted.x: KWDT-I gave its award in 1973, and its final award was issued in 1976.
accepted.tq: Separate the initial award year from the later final-award year.
accepted.sec: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

accepted.s: At 75 per cent dependability, which set of shares was awarded by KWDT-I to Maharashtra, Karnataka and the united Andhra Pradesh respectively?
accepted.x: KWDT-I awarded 560 TMC to Maharashtra, 700 TMC to Karnataka and 800 TMC to the united Andhra Pradesh at 75 per cent dependability.
accepted.tq: Use the fixed three-State numerical sequence and avoid swapping neighbouring entries.
accepted.sec: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

accepted.s: The united Andhra Pradesh share of 800 TMC under KWDT-I became 811 TMC when what was added?
accepted.x: The 800 TMC allocation, together with 11 TMC of return flows, produced the 811 TMC figure used in the ad hoc division.
accepted.tq: Test the small numerical component that explains the difference between two closely related totals.
accepted.sec: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal was chaired by Justice R.S. Bachawat and gave its award in 1980. KWDT-I was chaired by Justice R.S. Bachawat but its award dates were 1973 and 1976; KWDT-II was chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar and reported in 2010, with a further report in 2013.
accepted.tq: Check both the chairperson and award year in each pair rather than accepting a familiar name alone.
accepted.sec: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about KWDT-II:
1. It was chaired by Justice Brijesh Kumar.
2. Its award was made in 2010, with a further report in 2013.
3. It dealt with shared surplus and 65-per-cent-dependable flows.
4. Its award was notified and has not been challenged in the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: the KWDT-II award was not notified and was challenged in the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Find the false status statement by checking the distinction between an award being made, notified and challenged.
accepted.sec: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

accepted.s: According to the cited allocation record, the additional share attributed to Andhra Pradesh by KWDT-II was how much?
accepted.x: The cited allocation record places the additional Andhra Pradesh share under KWDT-II at 196 TMC.
accepted.tq: Test a precise allocation figure with close numerical alternatives.
accepted.sec: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

accepted.s: The Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal award of 1980 was based primarily on what?
o: A fresh 50:50 formula between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
accepted.x: The GWDT award of 1980 was based on inter-State agreements.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal basis of the award rather than confusing it with a later reorganisation arrangement.
accepted.sec: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

accepted.s: What is Andhra Pradesh’s stated position regarding the quantification of Godavari surplus under the GWDT award?
o: The surplus was quantified only by KWDT-II.
The entire surplus has already been quantified and divided equally.
The surplus is not yet quantified under the award.
The award expressly transferred the surplus to Telangana.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has stated that the Godavari surplus has not yet been quantified under the GWDT award.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an assertion about pending quantification from a completed allocation.
accepted.sec: Tribunals - chairperson, award year, shares

accepted.s: The Tungabhadra Board was set up under which enactment and provision?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Section 84
The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, Section 5
accepted.x: The Tungabhadra Board was established under Section 66 of the Andhra State Act, 1953.
accepted.tq: Use the parent-Act trap by distinguishing the original statutory basis from the later reorganisation law.
accepted.sec: Tungabhadra Board - parent Act, canals regulated

accepted.s: After the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh, which entities replaced the undivided Andhra Pradesh on the Tungabhadra Board?
accepted.x: After 2014, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana replaced the undivided Andhra Pradesh on the Tungabhadra Board under Section 91(1) of the AP Reorganisation Act.
accepted.tq: Track institutional succession after bifurcation and avoid substituting neighbouring basin States.
accepted.sec: Tungabhadra Board - parent Act, canals regulated

accepted.s: Which of the following canals or schemes continue to be regulated by the Tungabhadra Board under Section 91(2)?
o: High Level Canal, Low Level Canal and Rajolibanda Diversion Scheme
Right Main Canal, Left Main Canal and Polavaram Canal
Srisailam Canal, Nagarjuna Sagar Canal and RDS only
Kakatiya Canal, RDS and Dowleswaram Canal
accepted.x: The Tungabhadra Board continues to regulate releases to the High Level Canal, Low Level Canal and Rajolibanda Diversion Scheme.
accepted.tq: Match the statutory Board with the specific canals and scheme under its continuing regulation.
accepted.sec: Tungabhadra Board - parent Act, canals regulated

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the purposes for which KWDT’s term was extended under Section 89?
o: Addressing project-wise and operational issues within the scope of the reference
Automatically dividing the undivided Andhra Pradesh share between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
Fixing an operational protocol for releases during deficit flows
Making project-wise allocations where no tribunal had done so
accepted.x: Section 89 covered project-wise allocation where necessary and an operational protocol for deficit flows. It did not itself automatically divide the Andhra Pradesh share between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the express terms of a statutory reference from a later political or legal demand.
accepted.sec: KWDT-II - AP-Telangana allocation dispute, Section 89 reference

accepted.s: Under Section 89, the operational protocol to be fixed by KWDT primarily concerned releases during which situation?
o: Periods after completion of every new project
Floods in the Godavari basin only
accepted.x: Section 89 provided for fixing an operational protocol for releases during deficit flows.
accepted.tq: Identify the hydrological condition directly connected with the statutory operational protocol.
accepted.sec: KWDT-II - AP-Telangana allocation dispute, Section 89 reference

accepted.s: What was Andhra Pradesh’s position regarding the party structure in the KWDT-II proceedings?
o: Telangana should replace all other parties to the dispute.
Only the Union Government should be made a party.
Telangana should be added as a separate party so that allocation could be redone among four States.
The proceedings should be confined to the Godavari basin.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh wanted Telangana to be added as a separate party so that allocations could be reconsidered among four States.
accepted.tq: Test the requested procedural change and its stated consequence separately from the later terms of reference.
accepted.sec: KWDT-II - AP-Telangana allocation dispute, Section 89 reference

accepted.s: In October 2023, the Centre gave KWDT-II further terms of reference under which provision to divide the Andhra Pradesh share between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
o: Section 91(2) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
Section 84(3) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
Section 89 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 alone
Section 5(1) of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956
accepted.x: In October 2023, the Centre gave KWDT-II further terms of reference under Section 5(1) of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, for dividing the Andhra Pradesh share between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
accepted.tq: Use the wrong-section trap by separating the AP Reorganisation Act provisions from the ISRWD Act provision.
accepted.sec: KWDT-II - AP-Telangana allocation dispute, Section 89 reference
